text: Where should the right to rule come from?
From the citizens' will
From the competence or the strength of those who govern
From a traditional, religious or hereditary order
From nowhere: as little rule as possible, or I do not know
How should citizens exercise that right?
By electing representatives and parties
By deciding for themselves, directly
Organized by work and community, without classes
What kind of representative system?
Elected representatives under a constitution, with guaranteed rights
Parties that control the state and the choice of offices
A symbolic monarch, with an elected government
How should people decide directly?
In assemblies and in-person referendums
By online voting and digital platforms
In self-governing local communities, joined in a confederation
What form of collective organization?
Workers' councils, elected from the bottom up
Common ownership and the end of social classes
What gives the right to govern?
Technical knowledge, applied with data
Merit proven in exams, results and careers
Management as in a company, answering to those who sustain the state
Strength and discipline
Who should wield that force?
The armed forces, with the military hierarchy
One person in command, with no limits that control them
Which traditional order?
A monarch with total power
Noble families or a traditional elite
Religion, with religious leaders and sacred law
A monarch chosen and kept by voluntary contract, with no compulsory state
Which of these sentences comes closest to what you think?
No government at all, only voluntary agreements among people
A minimal state: only security, justice and defense
I have no clear preference about who should govern

name: Theocracy
description: Government rests on the authority of a religion: religious leaders or sacred law have the final word.

name: Absolute monarchy
description: A hereditary monarch rules with total power, above the laws and parliaments.

name: Autocracy
description: Power concentrated in a single person, with no free elections and no limits to control it.

name: Anarchism
description: A society without a central government, organized by voluntary agreement and the self-rule of communities.

name: Partocracy
description: Parties control the state and decide who holds office; power circulates among party machines.

name: Representative democracy
description: Citizens elect representatives who govern for a limited time, under a constitution that protects rights.

name: Direct democracy
description: Citizens themselves decide laws and major questions, in assemblies, plebiscites and referendums.

name: Councils
description: Power comes from councils of workers and communities, built from the bottom up, with recallable mandates.

name: Communalism
description: Society is organized in self-governing local communities that decide by assembly and join in a confederation.

name: Digital democracy
description: Citizens vote and propose laws on digital platforms, with direct and continuous participation online.

name: Constitutional monarchy
description: A monarch is head of state, but government works within a constitution and through elected representatives.

name: Minarchism
description: The state is limited to the minimum: security, justice and defense, and nothing more.

name: Meritocracy
description: Leadership posts go to those who stand out in exams, results and careers, not by vote or inheritance.

name: Technocracy
description: The state is run by technical experts, who decide on the basis of data and competence.

name: Stratocracy
description: Power rests with the armed forces, and military discipline and hierarchy organize the state.

name: Aristocracy
description: Power rests with a class of noble or traditional families, who rule by birth, honor and duty.

name: Anarcho-monarchism
description: A monarch chosen and kept voluntarily, by contract, with no compulsory state.

name: Neocameralism
description: The state is run like a sovereign company, by managers who answer to those who sustain it and to those who choose to live in it.

name: Communism
description: A classless society, with the means of production held in common and decisions taken collectively.

name: Balanced
description: No settled position on who should have the final say over the country's course.
